title: Lovett
author: Lucy Roslyn
tagline: You may think you already know Mrs Lovett.

synopsis: Newly widowed, Mrs Lovett needs to find a way to survive. Using skills learned from a whaler father, a courtesan mother and a butcher husband, Eleanor "recalibrates" her life - and her relationship with God. An origin story set before her infamous partnership with Sweeney Todd.

cast.name: Lucy Roslyn
cast.note: Written and performed by. Co-founder and Creative Director of BoonDog Theatre.

content_warnings.headline: Violence and death
content_warnings.detail: References to violence, killing, butchery and the handling of human remains.

content_warnings.headline: Age guidance 14+
content_warnings.detail: Recommended for ages 14 and above. The Criterion advises caution but does not enforce an age limit.

content_warnings.headline: Bereavement and grief
content_warnings.detail: The play opens on a recent widowhood and returns to loss throughout.

content_warnings.headline: Poverty and destitution
content_warnings.detail: Sustained depiction of hunger, debt and the choices poverty forces.

content_warnings.headline: References to sex work
content_warnings.detail: Eleanor's mother was a courtesan; the play discusses sex work without depicting it.

content_warnings.headline: Religious content
content_warnings.detail: Eleanor's relationship with God is central, and is treated with irreverence as well as seriousness.

content_warnings.headline: Opens in darkness
content_warnings.detail: The performance begins in a full blackout, with sound only, for around a minute.
content_warnings._note: Not a content warning so much as a sensory one - useful for anxious patrons and for anyone arriving late. Jamie may prefer it cut so the opening lands cold; it is flagged as optional in the copy deck.

content_warnings.headline: No interval
content_warnings.detail: The play runs straight through for approximately 70 minutes.

writer.body: Co-founder and Creative Director of BoonDog Theatre. Lovett premiered at the Edinburgh Festival Fringe in 2025 and has toured the UK ever since - including a preview at the Belgrade, just down the road, in July 2025.
writer.footline: Written and performed by Lucy Roslyn

director.quote: Everyone arrives thinking they know who Mrs Lovett is. The play happens in the gap between that and who she actually was.

about_play.headline: Morality becomes a moveable feast
about_play.body: You may think you already know Mrs Lovett, but this new play explores what made her: the brutal choices and disappointments of a life in poverty. When the difference is life or death, morality becomes a moveable feast - and Eleanor is getting hungry...

staging.headline: One performer
staging.body: A butcher's block, a whetstone, a knife, a cup, a hunk of bread. Everything else is Eleanor.

venue.body: The Criterion has staged over 450 productions since 1955, in a building that is over 140 years old - an 1884 Methodist chapel that became a theatre in 1960. It is run entirely by its members: no paid employees, on stage or off.
venue.footline: Registered charity 1161430 • A volunteer-run theatre in Earlsdon, Coventry

volunteer.body: Actors, makers, technicians, front-of-house, bar and box office - every part of the Criterion is volunteer-run, and new members are always welcome. No experience needed to get involved on stage, backstage, or around the building.

press_quotes.quote: One of the most relentless, compelling pieces of work at the Fringe... An extraordinarily powerful hour.
An entirely disarming performance, precise, committed and unflinching... This production is one that you can really sink your teeth into.
This brilliant script, paired with even more powerful acting, had me mesmerised... As exciting and captivating as the biggest of productions.

_press_quotes_note: Exact wording lifted from the Criterion event page (criteriontheatre.co.uk/event/10652), where the venue is already using them - i.e. cleared for promotional use.
